title: How to write error messages that actually help users rather than frustrate them
summary: Five principles for user-facing error copy: identifying error types, plain conversational language, avoiding whimsy, active voice, and consistent next-step guidance.
when-to-read: Read when writing or reviewing user-facing error messages, or establishing UX-writing/design-system conventions for them. Do not read for internal log message or exception-string conventions aimed at engineers (see logging best practices) — this is about end-user-facing copy.
